title: Donald Trump says PH, US clinch 'big' trade deal
summary: US President Donald Trump on Wednesday announced that the Philippines and the United States had secured a “big” trade deal as the two leaders held bilateral talks in Malacañang.

blocks.text: US President Donald Trump on Wednesday announced that the Philippines and the United States had secured a “big” trade deal as the two leaders held bilateral talks in Malacañang.

“We've just consummated a very big trade deal, the biggest trade deal we've ever made by far, and it's a fair deal for both countries, and we're very happy with it,” Trump said during a state luncheon at Malacañang.
“I'm proud to say that we're making the alliance between the United States and the Philippines much stronger than it's ever been before, especially with the consummation of this deal,” he added.
Trump did not provide further details about the trade agreement.
Meanwhile, Philippine Ambassador to the United States Jose Manuel “Babes” Romualdez said the deal involves food and energy supply.
“The US offered for us to diversify our food supply and energy requirements,” he said.

In his remarks at the luncheon, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said the Philippines and the United States continued to strengthen their partnership in trade, investment, energy, technology, resilience, supply chains and education, among other areas.

“I am confident that your visit will give fresh momentum to our partnership and open new opportunities for our two countries to work even more closely together for our peoples, for our region, for the peace and prosperity that we all seek,” Marcos said.
Trump is in the Philippines from Nov. 17 to 18. He arrived late Tuesday afternoon to attend the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and Related Summits.
His visit has drawn protests from various groups across the country, particularly over the proposed Pax Silica initiative.— MCG, GMA News
